name: Draught flask
description:
The shared vessel every draught is served in: a round-bottomed flask under a chitin stopper, filled two thirds. The glass is drawn behind the fluid rather than over it — a translucent pane across the liquid washes the colour out, and on these the colour IS the identity, so the pane is a highlight streak instead. Each fluid is a variant, which is what keeps eight draughts one family: a change to the flask changes all of them at once. What tells the eight apart is not the flask but what is suspended in it — specks, bubbles, pulp, lumps, crystals, grit, flakes, eggs. Those are authored per draught rather than composed from the library, because nothing in the library is a lump of sediment; the flask is the only part they share, and it is this document. That division is the point: a draught is one variant of this plus one handful of solids. Note for whoever picks this up next: `description` and `name` are gallery and manifest copy — a consuming game reads ids, geometry and animation names, never these — so a pass that only rewrites them changes nothing downstream. The pin in the game is deliberately **not** being moved for it.

Not in use. The draughts were drawn for a roster the game decided against — it keeps the eight shells, and a run varies by which body you are rather than by what it drank. Everything built on this flask is therefore unadopted art: `ss.draught.*` and `ss.char.survivor`. Kept, not deleted, because the drawing is the only place the idea survives in full, and because nothing downstream asks for these, so nothing downstream breaks by their staying.
